Three ants walk on a thin rod 100 cm long.
When an ant reaches either end of the rod it falls off. When two ants meet,
they BOUNCE: both instantly reverse direction, and each keeps its own speed.

Starting positions and velocities (positive = toward the 100 cm end):

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s
- Ant B: at 40 cm, moving -1 cm/s
- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s

After how many seconds does the LAST ant fall off the rod? Give the exact
number of seconds.


When you are finished, output your final answer on its own line, as the last line of your response, in the exact format:
ANSWER: <your answer>

text:
The ants have fixed speed magnitudes 3,1,2. Simulate collisions in order.

Initial $t=0$: A=10,+3; B=40,-1; C=80,-2.

A and B approach at relative speed 4 over distance 30, so meet at
$t=7.5$ at $10+3(7.5)=32.5$.
Then A=-3, B=+1, C at $80-2(7.5)=65$ with -2.

Now A heads left to 0: distance 32.5 at 3 needs $65/6$.
B at 32.5 heading +1 and C at 65 heading -2 approach at speed 3
over distance 32.5, needs $65/6$.

So at $t=7.5+65/6=55/3$:
A reaches 0 and falls off, while B and C meet at
$32.5+65/6=130/3$.

Then B reverses +1 to -1, C reverses -2 to +2.

B heads left from $130/3$ at 1: needs $130/3$ more, falls at
$55/3+130/3=185/3$.
C heads right from $130/3$ at 2: needs $85/3$ more, falls at
$55/3+85/3=140/3$.

The last to fall is B at $185/3$ s.

ANSWER: 185/3
